- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism; especially after recent spikes.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, apply a “lagged mean reversion” rule: subtract 10–15% of the peak from next period’s forecast if sentiment turns bearish or neutral.
- In high-event periods (≥5 events/30d), model tends to overestimate supply impact; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to historical mean for same event count.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 1.00), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average (EMA) to smooth forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast mean, check for “overshoot after spike” — if forecast peaked too high, reduce next 3–5 periods by 5–10% to align with observed mean reversion.
- In low-event periods (≤3 events/30d), model tends to underestimate volatility; increase forecast variance by 1–2% to account for sentiment noise or policy uncertainty.
